paragraphs.source_en: All day long, Okō never left the brazier, silently embroidering a small handkerchief. She had learned the craft from her aunt. Myōshū, the mother of Hon'ami Kōetsu, was still hale and hearty and lived in Kyoto. Though now past sixty, she still refused to wear silk, clothing herself only in cotton and hemp. She said that excessive luxury was a violation of the teachings of the great saint Nichiren.
